title: Inbound Signal Decoder & Priority Routing for Hosted Chat, Streaming and Tool Calls
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit heterogeneous Hosted API requests (chat + streaming + tool/function chains + structured outputs) to Product and Support. Current intake is inconsistent: PRDs and engineering signals are noisy, product triage requires manual interpretation of customer intent, and requests get prioritized based on ad-hoc heuristics. This causes missed SLA-driven requests, late enterprise ramp, and unclear roadmap trade-offs.

Goal: Define an "Inbound Signal Decoder" and Priority Routing lifecycle that converts raw customer requests into a deterministic priority score and a routing decision (self-serve backlog, product incubate, enterprise fast-track, or dedicated-engagement). The system should surface the top signals for hosted chat/streaming/toolcalls/structured-output features, be auditable for sales/solutions teams, and integrate with existing intake workflows (Zendesk/Salesforce -> Confluence -> Linear).

Scope: Non-bug feature intake only. Focus on hosted API surface: chat streaming behavior, tool/function calling guarantees, structured output schemas (JSON/Protobuf), and enterprise-specific requirements (SLA, data residency, observability hooks). Deliverables: taxonomy of signals, a priority scoring rubric, routing rules, an intake form template for customer facing teams, and a small automation that suggests initial priority in Linear via labels and score metadata.
discussion: 2026-03-05 - Alyssa Chen: Kickoff with GTM and Solutions engineering. Collected 12 recent enterprise requests across sales + support; common asks: streaming truncated outputs, tool call auth patterns, structured JSON output validation, and higher bandwidth SLA for realtime chat.

2026-03-07 - Marcus O'Hara: Eng sync. Feasibility notes from runtime team: streaming consistency vs. batching trade-offs; some requests require per-tenant KV cache pinning and specialized model variants. Engineering asks for classification to surface: latency-sensitive vs throughput-optimized, schema-strict vs schema-flexible, single-turn vs multi-turn tool chains.

2026-03-09 - Priya Raj (Solutions Eng): Shared two customer threads (ACME Corp & NovaHealth) highlighting regulatory needs and audit log requirements; recommended adding 'compliance burden' as a signal in scoring.

2026-03-10 - Design (Leah Kim): Proposed intake form wireframe; request body fields to capture example prompts, expected tokens/streaming window, tool call graph, and reference schema. Also proposed a compact summary card used in Linear to speed review.

2026-03-11 - Data (Ravi Patel): Suggested telemetry signals to correlate customer-reported issues with product metrics (95th percentile latency on chat-stream, rate of tool call failures, structured-output schema mismatches logged by validation pipeline).
2026-03-12 - Alyssa Chen: Drafted priority rubric and routing rules; posted to Confluence and asked for review from Product, Eng, Solutions, and Sales.
decisions: Use a weighted score (0-100) composed of signals: customer_size(20), SLA_need(25), implementation_complexity(15), security_compliance(15), revenue_urgency(15), telemetry_signal(10).

Requests scoring >=75 => enterprise fast-track review with dedicated PM/SE; 50-74 => product incubation candidate (prioritized in next roadmap cycle); <50 => backlog/self-serve with template responses and docs.
Add 'schema-strict' flag for structured output requests; schema-strict requests must include example payloads and automated schema validation test cases before engineering intake.
Integrate scoring automation such that when intake form is submitted a suggested priority label and score are added to the Linear issue; PM triage can override with justification.
Runtime team will provide a short feasibility matrix mapping feature types to likely required infra changes (KV pinning, quantized model variant, autoscale reservation).
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy and signal definitions published in Confluence with examples for chat, streaming, toolchains, and structured outputs.
Priority scoring rubric implemented as a lightweight Google Sheet and a first-pass automation that annotates Linear issues with score and routing label.
Intake form (Sales/Support facing) wireframe and copy completed and approved by Design and Solutions Eng.
Three pilot customer requests (one per signal archetype) processed through the new pipeline and outcomes reviewed with stakeholders.
Routing decision runbook documented and linked to escalation contacts for enterprise fast-track.
Telemetry mapping doc created with at least three automatable metrics for correlating request scores with runtime indicators.
